lessons.question: When a full-body actor's lower limbs are a dark material on a dark support, what owns their readable silhouette in the source: a value step of the garment material against its support, an owned edge/rim, or local light?

source_evidence.observed: light support (runner, also NUCLEAR_0083 farm): trousers ARE the darkest mass, near/far legs split by two darks, light ankle band separates shoe. Dark support (SOLAR suited figures, maroon interior): figure masses are raised ABOVE the environment value; darkest role belongs to the environment; near masses lighter than far. No outlines in either.

lessons.root_cause: missing operation: IF the actor's support/environment value is dark (night interior, space)
lessons.incorrect_operation: garment limb fills chosen as fixed dark swatches regardless of support value
lessons.corrected_operation: engine/lib/style.mjs#separate: new op; cast/keeper.mjs#limbSupportContrast: legs/sleeves pass through separate(material, support, ctx.param)
positive_construction_ops: pass every garment limb fill through separate(material, supportRole, ctx.param('style.limbSupportContrast')) — near limb at the full threshold, far limb at ~0.78×; keep the environment as the darkest role
lessons.regression_boundary: light supports (BRAIN_0386-type fields): dark trousers are the intended anchor — do not raise them; not a rule about faces, props or non-garment materials

lessons.question: When an actor holds a luminous prop at the moment of their reaction, how is the prop positioned relative to the face so both the object's change and the face's response stay legible: offset to a separate region, or overlapping?

source_evidence.observed: couch (light, relaxed): held prop raised ABOVE the face in its own region, face fully readable. lab (dark, attentive): object of attention sits in a separate lower region, both faces turned/gazing down to it; prop silhouette never overlaps a face plane; gaze line links them.

lessons.root_cause: missing operation: IF a held prop's change and the holder's reaction are read together
lessons.incorrect_operation: presentation target chosen in world space without testing the prop silhouette against the face plane
lessons.corrected_operation: films/_foundation_test/scenes/room_common.mjs#RAISE: targets moved to a forward presentation region; gaze poses aimed at the star
positive_construction_ops: choose the held-prop target so its silhouette clears the face bbox by ≥30 px on the gaze side; aim head + pupils at the prop centre (gaze links the two regions)
lessons.regression_boundary: deliberate concealment/reveal gags where the prop is meant to hide the face

lessons.question: When an older acting face carries a moustache at medium scale, how is the upper-lip/mouth region constructed so the expression stays readable: moustache value contrast against the face, separate visible mouth shape below it, and how much gap?

source_evidence.observed: farm (moustache): moustache = darkest face mark (hair value), compact bar; mouth a separate small dark shape BELOW it with a skin gap; nose small darker wedge above. clinic (no facial hair, unlike): mouth sits directly under the nose region. Grey-haired identity can keep light hair while the facial-hair mass separates by value.

lessons.root_cause: missing operation: IF facial hair covers the mouth region of an ACTING_CUE face
lessons.incorrect_operation: facial-hair fill taken from the light hair colour; mouth drawn under the facial hair
lessons.corrected_operation: engine/authoring/construct.mjs#separateFrom: value-separation op; films/_qual_A/subjects/engineer.mjs#facialHair: moustache fill + mouth geometry
positive_construction_ops: facial-hair fill passes separateFrom(skin, >=2.2) before geometry; mouth is authored as a separate dark shape below it with a skin gap
lessons.regression_boundary: faces without facial hair; distant/REDUCED_ICON faces where the mouth is not an acting cue; dark facial hair already separated
